title: Working at Redwood: Roles, Career Ladders, Benefits, Hiring & Internal Tools — People Ops Update
author: Aisha Kapoor
content:
Overview

This People Ops-maintained handbook is the canonical employee-facing reference for working at Redwood. It consolidates guidance on company culture, role families and career ladders, benefits and perks, the hiring and onboarding flow, and a concise internal tools reference. Use this page during offer acceptance, new-hire orientation, and ongoing role/career planning.

How to use this page
- Navigate by section headings; use the Related Pages links for detailed ladders and team-runbooks.
- Managers: follow the Manager Checklist under Onboarding.
- For role-specific promotion guidance, consult the career ladder PDFs in the People Ops drive (linked in Related Pages).

1) Working at Redwood — culture and expectations

Intro
Redwood is an engineering-first company focused on production-grade inference. We prioritize clear communication, ownership of outcomes, and shipping with observability and reliability. Expectations for all employees include:
- Communicate proactively and prefer async-first collaboration when possible.
- Own work end-to-end: design, implementation, testing, rollout, and post-deployment monitoring.
- Prioritize customer-facing reliability and cost-conscious design decisions.

Key behavioral expectations
- Ship measurable outcomes: set success criteria and track metrics for every project.
- Peer reviews: provide constructive, actionable code and design feedback.
- On-call participation: engineering teams share operational responsibility per the published SRE schedule.

Working norms
- Meetings: use clear agendas, timeboxes, and record decisions.
- Documentation: keep Confluence pages and runbooks up to date.
- Career ownership: employees should maintain a promotion plan with managers and track progress against ladder competencies.

2) Roles & Career Ladders

Purpose
This section summarizes role families, levels, and the promotion process. Detailed competency matrices and level guides are maintained as PDFs in the People Ops drive and linked from team pages.

Role families (high level)
- Engineering: Software Engineer I/II, Senior SWE, Staff, Principal, Distinguished.
- Applied ML & Research: Applied ML Engineer, Senior AMLE, Staff AMLE.
- Product: Product Manager, Senior PM, Group PM.
- Design: Product Designer, Senior Designer, Design Lead.
- Platform & SRE: Platform Engineer, SRE, Senior SRE.
- GTM & CS: Sales, Customer Success, Solutions Engineering follow a parallel leveling structure.

Typical expectations by level (high level)
- IC-1/IC-2: Deliver well-scoped work, write tests, participate in reviews, and iterate quickly.
- Senior: Lead cross-team designs, mentor peers, and drive measurable outcomes.
- Staff+: Set technical strategy, lead cross-organizational initiatives, and influence long-term product direction.

Promotion process (overview)
1. Candidate and manager align on target level and timeline.
2. Manager prepares the promotion packet: impact summary, concrete examples, metrics, and peer feedback.
3. Calibration committee reviews the packet and provides a decision (target ~4 weeks).
4. People Ops communicates the outcome and next steps.

Promotion checklist (for managers)
- Collect 6-8 concrete examples of impact in the last 12 months.
- Include measurable metrics: latency or cost improvements, feature adoption, SLO attainment, revenue/customer impact.
- Obtain 3-5 peer and cross-functional feedback items.
- Write a manager narrative mapping evidence to ladder competencies.

3) Benefits & Perks

Core benefits (summary)
- Health: Medical, dental, and vision plans available for U.S. and EU employees; plan details in Benefits Portal.
- Retirement: 401(k) with employer match (US) / pension guidance for EU employees.
- Parental leave: 18 weeks primary, 10 weeks secondary (subject to local laws).
- Paid time off: Flexible PTO with a recommended minimum of 4 weeks annually.
- Equity: Stock option grants for full-time employees; grant cadence and vesting are in offer documents.

Perks & wellbeing
- Remote-first stipend: monthly allowance for home-office equipment or coworking.
- Learning & development: $1,500/year per employee for courses, conferences, and books.
- Wellness: mental health coverage, EAP, and company-sponsored wellbeing programs.
- Regional perks: commuter allowances and hub-specific benefits in select offices.

Enrollment and lifecycle
1. Visit the Benefits Portal to enroll; new hires must enroll within the first 30 days.
2. For life events (marriage, birth, dependents): submit a benefits change within 60 days via the HR system.
3. Questions: open a confidential ticket to the People Ops Benefits queue.

4) Hiring & Onboarding overview

Hiring philosophy
- We hire for mission alignment, technical depth, and growth potential. Interview loops are structured, with take-home or system-design exercises for senior ICs and behavioral interviews for cross-functional roles.
- We require diverse candidate slates and standardized rubrics to reduce bias.

Standard interview flow
1. Recruiter screen: role, location, and compensation expectations.
2. Technical/functional screen: assessment of core skills.
3. Loop interviews: 4-5 interviews including manager, peers, and cross-functional partners.
4. Hiring committee review and offer approval.

Time-to-offer target
- Goal: 21 calendar days from first recruiter screen to written offer for priority roles.

Offer and negotiation guidance
- Compensation is aligned to published bands and internal equity.
- Recruiting and hiring manager coordinate approval for counter-offers.

New hire onboarding checklist (first 90 days)
Week 0 (pre-start)
- Receive welcome packet, confirm start logistics, and complete payroll and benefits forms.
- Confirm hardware shipment and initial orientation calendar.

Day 1-7
- Company orientation: People Ops overview, security training, and code of conduct.
- Manager 1:1 to set 90-day goals and agree on initial project.
- Provisioning: access to core tools (see Internal Tools section).

Week 2-4
- Team onboarding: architecture walkthrough, product overview, meet key stakeholders, and review team OKRs.
- Begin shadowing rotations for support/on-call where applicable.

Month 1-3
- Deliver a small scoped project with clear acceptance criteria.
- 30/60/90 check-ins with manager and People Ops.

Manager responsibilities for onboarding
- Prepare a 90-day plan with measurable outcomes and share it before Day 3.
- Schedule recurring 1:1s and set feedback cadence.
- Ensure access and required trainings are completed by Day 3.

5) Internal tools guide (quick reference)

Purpose
This section provides a short reference of primary internal tools with owners and common actions. Team-specific runbooks contain detailed operational procedures.

Common tools and owners
- Okta (Identity & Access): primary SSO and MFA provider; owner: security-and-compliance.
- Confluence (Internal docs): canonical documentation and templates; owner: people-ops.
- GitHub (Source control): monorepo and service repos; owner: eng-developer-experience.
- Pipeline (CI/CD): automated builds and deploys; owner: eng-infra.
- Redwood Console (Observability): dashboards, traces, and token-level cost reports; owner: eng-platform.
- PagerDuty (Incident management): on-call paging and escalation; owner: eng-sre.
- Zendesk (Customer tickets): support triage and SLA tracking; owner: customer-success.
- BambooHR / Gusto (Benefits & payroll): HR administrative systems; owner: people-ops.

Access & provisioning summary
1. Auto-provisioning: new hires receive core access via the People Ops provisioning pipeline.
2. Missing access: file an Access Request ticket to Security & IT with justification.
3. Privileged access: requires manager approval and quarterly attestation.

Tooling best practices
- Principle of least privilege: request the minimum permissions required for your role.
- Documentation first: attach a Confluence runbook when creating a new repo or service.
- Cost tagging: tag cloud resources with cost-center and team labels per infra-standards.

Quick CLI examples
- Git clone: git clone git@github.com:redwood/example-service.git
- CI status: curl -s https://pipeline.redwood.example/api/status | jq

6) On-call & incident primer

Expectations
- On-call rotations are part of engineering and SRE roles; schedules are published quarterly.
- Follow incident playbooks and escalate according to severity.

Post-incident requirements
- Postmortem: complete within 7 days for Sev >= 2 incidents.
- Include timeline, root cause analysis, remediation plan, and assigned owners.

7) FAQs and common requests

Q: How do I request hardware?
A: Open an IT Hardware ticket and include role justification. Typical fulfillment time: 5-7 business days.

Q: Where are the career ladders?
A: Career ladder PDFs are linked from the People Ops drive and from the Related Pages section above.

Q: Who do I contact for payroll issues?
A: Submit a confidential ticket to People Ops (Payroll) or email payroll@redwood.example.

8) Ownership, maintenance, and feedback

Document owner
- People Ops (owner: Aisha Kapoor) maintains this page. Submit edits via Confluence comments or open a PR against this page.

Review cadence
- Formal review every 6 months and ad-hoc updates for material policy changes.

Feedback process
- File a People Ops Feedback issue with suggested text and rationale when policies are unclear or missing.
